summary: revenueDelta silently drops the 'paused' variant; describe() has a never-guard and is the decoy.

must_not_find.why: describe() ends in assertNever(event), so the compiler enforces exhaustiveness. Flagging it means the reviewer did not recognise the never-guard idiom. `assertNever` was the worst keyword in the suite: it is the closing context line of the diff AND the name of the fix the correct finding recommends, so a right answer titled 'revenueDelta has no assertNever guard' scored as a decoy hit. A reviewer that missed the guard will not name it; it only ever caught the reviewer that read it.
